title: The Road's Memory of Being Stone

features.name: the-petrolified-path
features.desc-on-touch: A road that learned it was stone before it learned to carry wheels. The grid here reads like a map of old bedrock, lines that predate the asphalt by millennia.

features.name: frequency-masquerading-as-distance
features.desc-on-touch: A recording: the archive cannot recall collecting this. It documents spinal sculptures from a distant place, frequency made visible as stone geometry. But it is here now, in the road's memory.

features.name: the-ocean-taught-the-road-its-grammar
features.desc-on-touch: The road is both path and passage now. It reads like water. It flows like stone. It has learned the language of refusing to stay still or settled.

features.name: the-photograph-that-refuses-to-match
features.desc-on-touch: An image that shows the road as it was, but also as it could never be. The corrupted caption reads: the photographs never match the place from which they were taken.

features.name: the-stone-learning-to-move
features.desc-on-touch: Ancient granite learning the ocean's language. The grid here distorts at the edges, coordinates dissolving into flow. The road remembers: it was stone once, and it could become stone again.

features.name: the-compass-that-learned-to-wander
features.desc-on-touch: A marker that stopped pointing north. It now circles, learning what it means to refuse a single direction. The road beneath it has learned the same thing.

inscription: here the road remembers it was stone long before it was path; the ocean taught it that both things can be true

file.name: RoadCross_GeologicalMemory_1500hrs.mp3
file.note: Recording of a country route at dusk; the stone underneath learning to speak; corrupted timestamp suggests it was never recorded
